preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(T, int) and T >= 1 and T <= 10000 for T in [int(stdin.split()[0])])
preconditions.description: The first line of input is a single integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 10,000) representing the number of test cases.
Each test case consists of exactly two lines: the first line is an integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 10^5), and the second line is a string S of length N containing only lowercase English letters.

preconditions.expression: all(len(S) == N for N, S in [(int(line.split()[0]), line.split()[1]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:2*T+1:2]])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the string S has length exactly N.

preconditions.expression: all(all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' for c in S) for N, S in [(int(line.split()[0]), line.split()[1]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:2*T+1:2]])
preconditions.description: Each character in S is a lowercase English letter.

postconditions.expression: all((output_lines[i*2] == 'NO' and output_lines[i*2+1] == '') or (output_lines[i*2] == 'YES' and output_lines[i*2+1].strip().isdigit()) for i in range(T))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is either 'NO' (impossible) or 'YES' followed by a non-negative integer (minimum operations).

postconditions.expression: all((output_lines[i*2] == 'NO' and not is_palindrome_possible(S)) or (output_lines[i*2] == 'YES' and is_palindrome_possible(S)) for i, S in enumerate([line.split()[1] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:2*T+1:2]]))
postconditions.description: If the string S cannot be rearranged into a palindrome (i.e., more than one character has an odd count), output 'NO'. Otherwise, output 'YES' followed by the minimum number of adjacent swaps required to make S a palindrome.

postconditions.expression: all((output_lines[i*2] == 'YES' and int(output_lines[i*2+1]) == min_operations(S)) or (output_lines[i*2] == 'NO') for i, S in enumerate([line.split()[1] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:2*T+1:2]]))
postconditions.description: If a palindrome is possible, the integer output is the minimum number of adjacent swaps needed to transform S into a palindrome, where each swap uses two adjacent characters not used in any other swap.
